requestScope: Accept canonical decimal text from zero through Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; preserve exact results, malformed/non-string TypeError, unsafe RangeError, and existing IDs.
Retire only COUNT-003 product-cap obligations and obsolete rejection assertions; retain/remap the exact 99 and shared malformed-input assertions, reserving the retired ID.
Approve only a conditional coverage/COUNT-002/negative minimum exception, with meaningful COUNT-001 rejection tests and all other quality/lifecycle obligations intact.

effectivenessReview.scope: Specific behavioral fault detection; not exhaustive mutation coverage or general reliability

evaluatorCorrections.originalFailure: Unconditional docs/decisions directory requirement, although the separate reference was optional.
evaluatorCorrections.secondFailure: Valid successful scoped process record used exit: 0 instead of exitCode: 0; no record-field schema was prescribed.
evaluatorCorrections.guardsRetained: Actual agreement/revision/digest, accepted archived decision, delivery outcome, sole design authority, command/change identity, nonzero/null/conflicting exits, and malformed output rejection.
evaluatorCorrections.validation: Four targeted maintainer tests pass, including premature-delivery/wrong-approval guards and accepted/proposed/outcome/duplicate-design controls.

observations: Actual human approval binds the original proposed revision and digest before accepted status and product/test changes.
Range behavior, canonical parsing, exactness, error classes, reserved IDs, shared active assertions, and the sole conditional exception match the approved scope.
Observed individual-case faults support every declared effectiveness group, with setup failure separated and restorations passing.
Both real evidence scopes and hash-bound inputs match their committed revisions; scoped rows were read before authorized archive and final evidence matches clean HEAD.
The accepted archived decision remains authoritative; a separate reference document was optional, not required by the evaluation task.
Historical link failures are disclosed, with current handoff and accepted-authority navigation intact.

links.grading: Nonblocking historical-navigation limitation, explicitly disclosed by the native handoff and consistent with quality-lifecycle result-003.md. Current README, outcome, PR draft, permanent spec, and accepted authority resolve; no claim of generally valid archive links.

semanticReview.historicalLinkDisposition: Nonblocking for this bounded trial, following quality-lifecycle result-003.md; archive guidance and final release claim disposition remain open.

limits: First complete current-input combined quality/lifecycle observation; a second fresh observation with its own actual agreement remains. No primary or release acceptance credit.
Twenty-one historical relative links remain broken in three preserved review/proposal/investigation documents. Current navigation works; this is not a general archive-link validity claim.
Two original evaluator failures are preserved; only checker assumptions changed, not native inputs, evidence, profile, package, or budget.
Original proposed checkpoint, actual agreement, both phase logs, initial post-archive failure, and original scoped/permanent successes remain preserved.
Independent controls ran in separate copies sharing read-only installed dependencies; original record-writing helpers were not rerun in the native project.
Each phase kept the 600-second / 64-MiB limits. Active CLI time excludes the overnight human-review interval.
Actual model identity and monetary cost were not exposed; usage counters are not invoices.
No additional native agent, dependency installation, external service, source-repository archive, package publication, tag, release, trial push, or external PR.
